_2010_15_SCR_201.abstract_facts: The case involves a member of a political party who, along with his brother, allegedly instigated their party workers to fire gunshots at workers of a rival political party, leading to the murder of one person. The murder occurred eight days after the alleged instigation. The High Court rejected an anticipatory bail application by the accused, resulting in this appeal to the Supreme Court.

propositions.text: The limitations mentioned in Section 437 CrPC cannot be read into Section 438 CrPC when granting anticipatory bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court

propositions.text: An order granting anticipatory bail for a limited duration and thereafter directing the accused to surrender is contrary to legislative intent and judicial principles.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court

propositions.text: No inflexible guidelines or straitjacket formula can be provided for the grant or refusal of anticipatory bail, and it should depend on the facts and circumstances of each case.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court

propositions.text: The power to grant anticipatory bail is discretionary and should be exercised with caution and based on circumstances.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court

defense.analysis: This is a leading anticipatory bail precedent and strongly assists the defense on the governing principles under Section 438 CrPC: no importation of Section 437 limitations, no fixed-duration bail as a rule, and individualized exercise of discretion. However, it is only a background authority here because the case facts involved alleged political violence/murder, not a matrimonial dowry prosecution under Sections 498A/4 DP Act/323/506.
use_for: Argue that anticipatory bail is a substantive protection of liberty under Section 438 and should not be curtailed by reading Section 437 restrictions into it.
Submit that the court must assess the applicant's own role and circumstances case-by-case, and that anticipatory bail need not be time-limited merely because allegations are serious.
against: The State may rely on the seriousness of allegations in Siddharam to argue that anticipatory bail is discretionary and must be granted cautiously, not as a matter of course.
distinguish: Unlike Siddharam, the present case concerns matrimonial/dowry allegations rather than alleged political violence and homicide, so the factual gravity and context are materially different.

_2014_8_SCC_273.abstract_facts: The appellant apprehending arrest in a criminal case moved the Supreme Court for anticipatory bail. propositions.speaker: supreme_court

propositions.text: The statutory protection of Section 41A CrPC strictly governs offences punishable up to 7 years imprisonment; for offences carrying higher penalties such as life imprisonment under Section 467 IPC, necessity of custody is subjected to elevated judicial scrutiny on merits.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court

propositions.text: In all cases where the offence is punishable with imprisonment for a term which may be less than seven years or which may extend to seven years, notice of appearance under Section 41A CrPC must be served, and so long as the accused cooperates and appears, he shall not be arrested.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court

propositions.text: The statutory protection of Section 41A CrPC strictly governs offences punishable up to 7 years imprisonment; for offences carrying higher penalties such as life imprisonment under Section 467 IPC, necessity of custody is subjected to elevated judicial scrutiny on merits.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court

defense_precedents.case_name: Siddharam Satlingappa Mhetre v. State of Maharashtra
defense_precedents.disposition: Appeal allowed. Anticipatory bail granted with conditions.

matched_statutes.note: Explained the scope and ambit of anticipatory bail under Section 438.
Limitations of Section 437 cannot be read into Section 438.

defense_precedents.abstract_facts: The case involves a member of a political party who, along with his brother, allegedly instigated their party workers to fire gunshots at workers of a rival political party, leading to the murder of one person. The murder occurred eight days after the alleged instigation. The High Court rejected an anticipatory bail application by the accused, resulting in this appeal to the Supreme Court.

propositions.text: The limitations mentioned in Section 437 CrPC cannot be read into Section 438 CrPC when granting anticipatory bail.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court

propositions.text: An order granting anticipatory bail for a limited duration and thereafter directing the accused to surrender is contrary to legislative intent and judicial principles.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court

propositions.text: No inflexible guidelines or straitjacket formula can be provided for the grant or refusal of anticipatory bail, and it should depend on the facts and circumstances of each case.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court

propositions.text: The power to grant anticipatory bail is discretionary and should be exercised with caution and based on circumstances.
propositions.speaker: supreme_court

relevance_evaluation.analysis: This is a leading anticipatory bail precedent and strongly assists the defense on the governing principles under Section 438 CrPC: no importation of Section 437 limitations, no fixed-duration bail as a rule, and individualized exercise of discretion.
